# pbs_realm_ad (Resource)

Manages an Active Directory realm of a Proxmox Backup Server: users sign in to PBS with the name and password of their Active Directory account, as `<sAMAccountName>@<realm>`. PBS looks the account up below `base_dn`, by `sAMAccountName`, and checks the password by binding as it.

Only users that exist in PBS can sign in: create them with `pbs_user`, or have a sync create them from the directory — in the web interface, or with `proxmox-backup-manager ad sync <realm>`; `filter`, `user_classes`, `sync_attributes` and `sync_defaults` shape what it does. They have no privileges until a `pbs_acl` grants them some.

~> **PBS checks the connection on every change.** Creating the realm, and every update — even of `comment` — first connects to the server as the realm would after the change, binds as `bind_dn` and reads `base_dn`; PBS saves nothing when that fails, and the apply fails with the reason. PBS connects from its own host, so the server must be reachable from there, not from where Terraform runs. A bind password changed in the directory but not in PBS blocks every update until a new `password_wo_version` sends the new one. Destroying the realm connects to nothing.

**The bind password** is write-only, `password_wo` with `password_wo_version`: PBS never returns it, so it stays out of the plan and state. PBS needs it to create a realm with a `bind_dn`, so creating one — or replacing one, after an import, say — without `password_wo` fails in the plan.

~> **Only one realm is the default.** `default = true` takes the flag from the realm that had it, the built-in `pam` and `pbs` and realms outside Terraform included. Set it on one realm only: two realms with `default = true` take it from each other on every apply.

Changing `realm` or `capath` replaces the realm. A new `capath` keeps the name, so such a replacement cannot use `create_before_destroy`: PBS refuses the new realm while the old one exists. PBS keeps the users of a deleted realm, and their ACL entries.

Managing realms needs `Realm.Allocate` on `/access/domains`; reading one `Sys.Audit` there.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Sign-in with Active Directory accounts, as <sAMAccountName>@ad, such as
# alice@ad: PBS looks the account up by sAMAccountName and checks the password
# by binding as it. PBS connects to a domain controller whenever the realm is
# created or changed — even just its comment — from the PBS host, not from
# where Terraform runs, and saves nothing when it cannot connect, bind as
# bind_dn and read base_dn: the apply fails with the reason.
resource "pbs_realm_ad" "ad" {
  realm   = "ad"
  server1 = "dc1.example.com"
  server2 = "dc2.example.com"
  comment = "Active Directory example.com"

  # LDAP over TLS, on port 636, with the domain controllers' certificates
  # checked against the system's certificate authorities, to which the
  # domain's own CA was added on the PBS host (update-ca-certificates); capath
  # names a CA certificate otherwise. mode = "ldap+starttls" uses port 389
  # instead.
  mode   = "ldaps"
  verify = true

  # The account PBS looks users up as, in UPN form; a distinguished name, such
  # as cn=pbs,cn=Users,dc=example,dc=com, works as well. Its password is
  # write-only: it never reaches the plan or state, and PBS receives it when
  # the realm is created, which needs it, and whenever password_wo_version
  # changes. Increment the version after changing the password in Active
  # Directory: PBS binds on every change, and fails while it has the old one.
  bind_dn             = "pbs@example.com"
  password_wo         = var.ad_bind_password
  password_wo_version = 1

  # No base_dn: PBS asks the domain controller for the domain's naming
  # context, dc=example,dc=com, when it creates the realm, and keeps it. Set
  # it to look users up below one organizational unit only.

  # Only users that exist in PBS can sign in: pbs_user creates them, or a sync
  # does — proxmox-backup-manager ad sync ad on the PBS host, or Sync under
  # Access Control > Realms in the web interface. The filter limits a sync to
  # the members of one group: otherwise it takes every entry that is a person
  # or user, computer accounts included. Without sync_attributes, it creates
  # users without email address or names, and leaves those of existing users
  # alone.
  filter = "(memberOf=cn=PBS Users,ou=Groups,dc=example,dc=com)"

  # The sign-in form preselects the realm. Only one realm is the default: set
  # it on one realm only.
  default = true
}

# A user of the realm, the domain account alice, who may manage the
# datastores.
resource "pbs_user" "alice" {
  userid = "alice@${pbs_realm_ad.ad.realm}"
  email  = "alice@example.com"
}

resource "pbs_acl" "alice" {
  path    = "/datastore"
  auth_id = pbs_user.alice.userid
  role    = "DatastoreAdmin"
}

variable "ad_bind_password" {
  description = "Password of the PBS service account in Active Directory."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `realm` (String) Realm name, 2 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`, and neither `pam` nor `pbs`, the built-in realms. Users of the realm are `<name>@<realm>`. Changing it replaces the realm.
- `server1` (String) Server PBS connects to: a host name or IPv4 address, or an IPv6 address in square brackets, without a port.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `base_dn` (String) Entry users are looked up below, such as `dc=example,dc=com`. When left out, PBS asks the server for its default naming context, the domain's root, when it creates the realm, and keeps that. PBS cannot remove it: removing `base_dn` keeps the one PBS has.
- `bind_dn` (String) Account PBS binds as to look users up, such as `cn=pbs,cn=Users,dc=example,dc=com` or, as a user principal name, `pbs@example.com`; requires a password, `password_wo`, when the realm is created. When left out, PBS searches anonymously, which Active Directory refuses by default.
- `capath` (String) Certificate authority PBS trusts for the server, a path on the PBS host: a PEM file, trusted besides the system's certificate authorities, or a directory of PEM certificates, all of which are trusted instead of them — any other file in it fails every connection. PBS reads it whenever it connects, even with `mode = "ldap"`, so it must exist. PBS can neither change nor remove it once the realm exists: changing or removing `capath` replaces the realm.
- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `default` (Boolean) Whether the sign-in form preselects this realm. Only one realm is the default: `true` takes the flag from the realm that had it. Defaults to `false`.
- `filter` (String) LDAP filter that limits which entries a sync turns into users, such as `(memberOf=cn=pbs,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com)`. Signing in does not use it. None when left out.
- `mode` (String) How PBS connects: `ldaps`, over TLS; `ldap+starttls`, plain LDAP that switches to TLS first; or `ldap`, the default, in plain text, in which the bind password and the passwords of users signing in cross the network unencrypted.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password of `bind_dn`, which it requires. Write-only: Terraform passes it to PBS without storing it in the plan or state, and PBS never returns it, so a change made outside Terraform goes unnoticed. PBS receives it when the object is created and whenever `password_wo_version` changes. Requires `password_wo_version`, and Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later. PBS needs it to create a realm with a `bind_dn`; removing it, with `password_wo_version`, keeps the password PBS has.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Version of `password_wo`, which Terraform stores in its place. Change it — increment it, say — to send a new `password_wo`; removing it, with `password_wo`, leaves the value on the server as it is. Requires `password_wo`.
- `port` (Number) Port of both servers, 1 to 65535. When left out, 636 with `mode = "ldaps"` and 389 otherwise.
- `server2` (String) Server PBS connects to when `server1` does not answer, in the same form. None when left out.
- `sync_attributes` (Attributes) LDAP attributes a sync takes users' properties from, at least one. A property left out is not synced: users keep theirs, unless `sync_defaults.remove_vanished` has `properties`, which removes it from every user a sync finds. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sync_attributes))
- `sync_defaults` (Attributes) What a sync does unless it is told otherwise when it is started, at least one option. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sync_defaults))
- `user_classes` (Set of String) Object classes a sync considers users: an entry is one when it has any of them. Defaults to `["inetorgperson", "person", "posixaccount", "user"]`.
- `verify` (Boolean) Whether PBS checks the server's TLS certificate, against the system's certificate authorities or `capath`. Defaults to `false`: with `ldaps` or `ldap+starttls` and without `verify`, PBS accepts any certificate, so the connection is encrypted but whoever answers in place of the server gets the passwords.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `realm`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.

<a id="nestedatt--sync_attributes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sync_attributes`

Optional:

- `email` (String) LDAP attribute holding the user's email address, such as `mail`.
- `firstname` (String) LDAP attribute holding the user's first name, such as `givenName`.
- `lastname` (String) LDAP attribute holding the user's last name, such as `sn`.


<a id="nestedatt--sync_defaults"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sync_defaults`

Optional:

- `enable_new` (Boolean) Whether a sync enables the users it creates, and the users it updates that have no enabled flag stored in PBS; PBS defaults to `true`. PBS stores none for an enabled user unless its creation sent `enable = true`: `pbs_user` does not send the default, and an update that enables a user removes the flag. So `false` disables the enabled users a sync finds, those `pbs_user` manages included, until the next apply enables them again. Disabled users stay disabled.
- `remove_vanished` (Set of String) What a sync removes when it no longer finds something in the directory: `entry` the users of the realm it does not find, with their API tokens — users Terraform manages included; `acl`, together with `entry`, the ACL entries of those users and their tokens, and alone nothing; `properties` the email address and names of users it finds that the directory has no value for, or that `sync_attributes` does not name. PBS removes nothing when left out.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_realm_ad.ad
  identity = {
    realm = "ad"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `realm` (String) Realm name, such as `ad`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_realm_ad.ad
  id = "ad"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Active Directory realms are imported by name. PBS never returns the bind
# password, so an import reads none, and PBS keeps the one it has: with
# password_wo and password_wo_version in the configuration, the next apply
# sends password_wo; without them, a plan that replaces a realm with a
# bind_dn — for a new realm name, or a new or removed capath — fails, as PBS
# needs the password to create it.
terraform import pbs_realm_ad.ad ad
```
